title: Aggregate economic stability coexists with financial strain, low institutional trust, mixed health, and declining cultural engagement in the UK
source_unit: UK Office for National Statistics, Beyond GDP insights, UK measures of National Well-being: June 2026
geography: United Kingdom national well-being measures, with some indicators for constituent nations or specific UK geographies; 59 annual and 7 quarterly headline measures

observations.period: April 2026; household finance and consumer sentiment

denominator.unit: UK adults and households represented across the ONS national well-being measures

financial_difficulty.unit: percent of adults finding it fairly or very difficult to get by financially

income_wealth.value: Income and wealth measures were broadly stable in the short term, with some inequality improvements

observations.method: ONS synthesis of 59 national well-being measures and seven quarterly headline measures from multiple official and non-official data sources.
observations.uncertainty: The bulletin combines measures with different populations, periods, geographies, definitions, and collection methods; aggregate stability does not describe every household's financial position.
observations.subgroup: UK adults, households, people in low income, consumers, workers, and groups experiencing unequal financial pressure.
observations.counterinterpretation: Stable income and wealth indicators can reflect genuine resilience, while financial difficulty and low confidence may reflect expectations, prices, debt, housing costs, or unequal exposure rather than aggregate income decline.

observations.period: March–April 2026; trust, civic voice, and community connection

denominator.unit: UK national well-being governance and relationships measures

government_trust.unit: percent of adults saying they tend to trust the UK government in March 2026

lack_of_say.unit: percent agreeing they have no say in what government does in April 2026

neighborhood_belonging.unit: percent reporting a sense of belonging to their neighborhood in April 2026

civic_change.value: Perceived influence improved compared with June 2025, but a clear majority still felt disconnected from government decision-making

observations.method: ONS national well-being framework combining survey measures of trust, civic influence, relationships, and neighborhood belonging.
observations.uncertainty: Measures are sensitive to timing, question wording, survey coverage, and events; the improvement in perceived influence occurred shortly before local elections and may not represent durable institutional change.
observations.subgroup: UK adults, local communities, voters, residents, public institutions, and people with different levels of political access or belonging.
observations.counterinterpretation: Low trust and weak perceived voice can coexist with strong local belonging and may motivate civic reform, local participation, or institutional repair rather than withdrawal alone.

observations.period: 2023–2026; health, relationships, time, and cultural participation

denominator.unit: UK adults across ONS health, relationship, time-use, and engagement measures

good_health.unit: percent of UK adults reporting good or very good health in early 2026

depression_anxiety.unit: percent of UK adults showing some evidence of depression or anxiety in January 2023 to December 2024

social_relationship_satisfaction.unit: percent satisfied with social relationships in September 2025

cultural_engagement.unit: percent engaging with arts and culture in October to December 2025, down from 90.0% the previous year

unpaid_work_gap.unit: minutes more unpaid work per day reported for women than men in March 2024

observations.method: ONS compilation of well-being, health, relationship, time-use, and arts-and-culture participation statistics with short- and long-term comparisons.
observations.uncertainty: The measures use different periods and sources; cultural engagement, mental-health indicators, and time-use gaps are not interchangeable or causal explanations of one another.
observations.subgroup: UK adults, people with mental-health difficulties, women and men with different unpaid-work burdens, cultural participants, and people experiencing loneliness or social support.
observations.counterinterpretation: High relationship satisfaction can provide resilience amid health and cultural-participation declines; reduced cultural engagement may reflect measurement timing, substitution into other activities, or access and cost pressures.

observations.period: 2024–2026; economy, work, environment, and public action

denominator.unit: UK national well-being economy and environment measures

gdp_per_head_change.unit: percent year-over-year increase in GDP per head in Q1 2026

consumer_confidence_index.unit: GfK Consumer Confidence Barometer in April 2026

government_trust.unit: percent tending to trust the UK government in March 2026

environmental_action.unit: percent of adults making at least some lifestyle changes to address environmental issues in March 2026

divergence.value: Improving GDP per head, slowing inflation, and stable labor-market conditions coexist with weak consumer confidence and low government trust

observations.method: ONS cross-domain national well-being comparison across economy, governance, environment, and public behavior measures.
observations.uncertainty: Cross-domain divergence is descriptive; it does not identify whether prices, expectations, institutions, health, political events, or distribution caused the sentiment gaps.
observations.subgroup: UK households, workers, consumers, voters, environmentally engaged adults, public institutions, and people exposed to unequal economic or environmental conditions.
observations.counterinterpretation: Low confidence and trust can coexist with environmental agency and improving aggregate output, indicating selective engagement rather than generalized disengagement.

related_sources.claim: ONS national well-being framework and dashboard context.
Complementary aggregate measurement frame connecting economic conditions to lived progress and thriving.

boundary: This record adds an official national well-being and beyond-GDP lens linking household financial room, consumer confidence, health, relationships, cultural participation, time, civic voice, institutional trust, environment, and public action. It uses aggregate and survey-based official statistics with mixed source quality, not a single respondent-level dataset, causal model, representative measure of every UK resident, or evidence that one domain caused another.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official ONS June 2026 bulletin reviewed for the 59-measure framework, financial difficulty, trust, civic voice, belonging, health, relationships, arts and culture, unpaid work, GDP per head, consumer confidence, and environmental action.
